slides.title: Introduction to OOP
content: OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) is a programming paradigm based on objects and classes
It organizes software design around real-world entities like objects instead of functions
Each object contains data (attributes) and behavior (methods)
It helps in writing modular, reusable, and maintainable code

slides.title: Why OOP is Needed
content: Procedural programming becomes complex for large applications
OOP provides better structure by dividing code into objects
It improves code reusability and reduces redundancy
It makes debugging and maintenance easier

slides.title: Class in OOP
content: A class is a blueprint or template for creating objects
It defines properties (variables) and behaviors (methods)
All objects created from a class share the same structure
Example: A 'Car' class can define color, speed, and methods like drive()

slides.title: Object in OOP
content: An object is an instance of a class
It represents a real-world entity with state and behavior
Each object has its own values for the properties
Example: A specific car like 'Red BMW' is an object of class Car

slides.title: Features of OOP
content: Encapsulation: Wrapping data and methods into a single unit
Inheritance: Acquiring properties from another class
Polymorphism: Same method behaving differently in different contexts
Abstraction: Hiding internal details and showing only functionality

slides.title: Encapsulation
content: Encapsulation means binding data and methods together in a class
It restricts direct access to data using access modifiers
Data is accessed using getter and setter methods
It improves security and data control

slides.title: Inheritance
content: Inheritance allows one class to inherit properties of another class
The parent class is called superclass and child is subclass
It promotes code reuse and hierarchical classification
Example: Animal → Dog inherits properties of Animal

slides.title: Polymorphism
content: Polymorphism means 'many forms'
A single method can perform different tasks based on context
It is achieved using method overloading and method overriding
Example: same function name but different parameters or behaviors

slides.title: Abstraction
content: Abstraction hides implementation details and shows only essential features
It reduces complexity by focusing on what an object does
It is achieved using abstract classes and interfaces
Example: Using a car without knowing engine internals

slides.title: OOP in Java
content: Java is a class-based, object-oriented programming language
Everything in Java revolves around classes and objects
It supports all OOP principles like inheritance and polymorphism
Programs start from the main method inside a class

slides.title: Real-Life Example of OOP
content: Class: Student (name, age, marks)
Object: Specific student like 'Rahul' with values
Encapsulation: Data hidden using private variables
Inheritance: GraduateStudent inherits Student properties

slides.title: Advantages of OOP
content: Code reusability using inheritance
Better data security using encapsulation
Flexibility using polymorphism
Easy maintenance and scalability of programs
